Before you start

  • The day before: check the PAT expiry date at the top of RUNBOOK.md and rotate the token if the demo is on or after the day before it. Run the RUNBOOK venue-network checklist: make warm from the venue network or the phone hotspot must end with "make warm: OK". Freeze the data: no make data, make load or make export from then on.
  • Half an hour before: from the repo root, make warm. It checks Snowflake auth first (auth or network errors are printed verbatim), resumes the engine, starts the warm query server and runs every hero query twice. It must end with "make warm: OK". The "ready" times it prints are what each act will take. Open the explorer on Overview and this script: open artifacts/deal_graph_explorer.html artifacts/demo_script.html. Do Not Disturb on, chat and mail closed, power connected, a large terminal font.
  • A quarter of an hour before: pre-launch the live session, cd demo_workspace && claude, accept the folder-trust and plugin prompts, and run one throwaway prompt (Run uv run python ask.py --list). Keep that session open. Keep a second terminal in demo_workspace/ for the fallback commands.
  • Ten minutes before: make warm again, because the engine suspends after half an hour idle. Then start make keepalive in its own terminal and leave it running until the Q&A ends. Type /clear in the live session.
  • During the demo: Claude Code is the main stage; the explorer is supporting evidence. Type /clear before each act's prompt and before the Finale prompt, never between a prompt and its follow-ups. Follow-ups come from demo_workspace/query_bank.md (SHOWCASE); keep it open beside this page. Paste prompts from this page with Copy; do not retype. If a typo lands, let it answer, or press Esc and paste again. While an act runs, talk through its business setup.
  • After the Q&A: Ctrl-C the keepalive terminal, then .venv/bin/python demo_workspace/ask.py --serve-stop and suspend the engine (RUNBOOK.md, "After the demo").
  • Say once, early: everything on screen is synthetic data about a fictional firm. Nothing is shown in Snowflake; Snowflake stores the data and runs RelationalAI.

The model

1 minExplorer: Global

Setup

One semantic layer over CRM, deal history, people and commercial data, living in your Snowflake. The knowledge graph holds 9,999 entities and 99,999 relationships; the explorer shows a 131-node slice with 187 edges, laid out the same way every time.

"These are your concepts: companies, sponsors, funds, intermediaries, people and their dated roles, deals, signals, CRM touches. The dashed boxes are not loaded from anywhere. Rules and graph algorithms derive them, and every derived fact points back to a rule you can read."

Explorer views: what you are looking at

Reference

One card per tab, in tab order. Rules means RelationalAI's rules reasoner (business logic written as derived facts). Graph means its graph reasoner (algorithms run over a network built from the model). Rules + Graph means a graph result feeds a rule, or the other way round, in the same model. Code names in small grey text are the rule ids in exports/rules.json; click any highlighted fact in the explorer to read that rule's docstring.

Overview Rules

Shows
The whole deal universe in one picture: our firm and people, targets, platforms, bankers, and how they connect. It answers "what is in the model" before any question is asked.
Read
Green: our firm and team. Blue: Tier A targets. Orange: platforms. Purple hexagon: intermediary. Grey: everything else. Edge colour is the relationship type, each with a toggle and count. Search, then expand one or two hops; click an edge and the side panel shows the rule that made it. The layout is a fixed picture computed at build time, not a reasoner output.
Uses
Who knows whom KNOWS: Tenure overlap K1_TENURE, board co-service K1_BOARD, deal co-participation K2_DEAL, positive CRM contact K3_CRM; current role EMPLOYMENT, ownership OWNERSHIP, commercial links COMMERCIAL.
Data: Person, Role (ROLE_HISTORY), TransactionParty, CommercialLink, Interaction (CRM_INTERACTION), Ownership. Shows 131 of 9,999 entities.
Not SQL
The edges are derived facts: a "knows" edge exists only where two dated tenures overlap, and no table holds it.

Scorecard Q-SCORE Rules

Shows
Fund IV targets ranked by thesis fit and readiness to transact now, and whether we already cover them. Every point traces to a named rule and dated evidence.
Read
Tier chip (A at 70+, B at 50+), stacked bar of blue Fit, orange Readiness, green Access, and a "No coverage" badge. Click a row for each component with points and evidence, then a component for its rule. The Finale toggle shows the re-score.
Uses
Sector-hierarchy closure, recursive SECTOR_CLOSURE; thesis fit and eligibility FIT_THESIS, EligibleTarget; fit points FIT_EBITDA, FIT_MARGIN; readiness components, capped at 50 R_CFO_FROM_PE, R_EXIT_WINDOW, R_BANKER, R_DEBT, R_SUCCESSION, R_NEW_DIRECTOR; access A_CRM; composite Score and Tier SCORE, ScoreComponent; known to CRM IN_CRM; why-not WHY_NOT. The Finale toggle adds warm-path points from the graph distance A_WARM_PATH, so that one view is Rules + Graph.
Data: Company, Sector, Region, FundFocus, Role (ROLE_HISTORY), Ownership, Signal (COMPANY_SIGNAL), PipelineEntry (PIPELINE), Interaction (CRM_INTERACTION).
Not SQL
Hierarchy recursion, dated multi-table signals and a per-point explanation in one governed definition; a keyword screen lets the decoys in.

Warm path Q-PATH Rules + Graph

Shows
For each top target, our warmest introduction route to the CEO (or the owner's board designee), hop by hop with dated evidence, or an honest "cold".
Read
Pick a target. Green: our people, where routes start. Large blue: the decision-maker. Thick blue line: warmest route; dashed grey: alternates; dashed red: a rejected claim (shared employer, no overlap); dashed red ring: no route. Edge labels carry the evidence; the side panel lists each hop and its rule.
Uses
Knows with tenure overlap, board, deal and CRM evidence KNOWS, K1_TENURE, K2_DEAL, K3_CRM; shared employer is not a tie SHARED_EMPLOYER_REJECT; decision-makers DECISION_MAKER; distance from our people with path reconstruction, at most 3 introductions, ranked by tie strength SEED_DISTANCE, WARM_PATH: distance(from_=seeds), distance(from_=decision-makers).
Data: Person, Role (ROLE_HISTORY), TransactionParty (TRANSACTION_PARTY), Interaction (CRM_INTERACTION), OurSeed, DecisionMaker.
Not SQL
Variable-length paths over a derived, time-qualified relationship; the shared-employer self-join reports introductions that never existed.

Deal flow Q-FLOW Rules + Graph

Shows
Which banks and boutiques actually bridge deal flow between founders and sponsors in our sectors, and which of them we barely call.
Read
Purple hexagons: intermediaries, sized by betweenness. Grey: sponsors and companies. Red ring: coverage gap. Node labels show our recent touchpoints. The table ranks betweenness, PageRank, deals in sector and touchpoints; "Compare with league table" shows the SQL deal count. The side panel lists the firm's deals.
Uses
Deal-flow scope, thesis deals closed 1996-01-01 to 2000-01-01 DEAL_FLOW_SCOPE; exact betweenness centrality plus PageRank DEAL_FLOW: betweenness_centrality, pagerank; CoverageGap, bridge rank 1 or better with at most 1 touchpoints COVERAGE_GAP; closest intermediary CLOSEST_INTERMEDIARY.
Data: Transaction, TransactionParty (TRANSACTION, TRANSACTION_PARTY), Intermediary, Sponsor, Role, Interaction (CRM_INTERACTION).
Not SQL
Centrality is a property of the whole network; GROUP BY gives a deal count, and volume is not control.

Conflict check Q-CONFLICT Rules + Graph

Shows
Before an IOI: does the bid subject trade with anything a Northwind fund owns today, and would our check breach Fund IV's thesis-area concentration guideline?
Read
Large blue: the bid subject. Solid red edge: conflict (a direct link to another fund's holding); dashed amber: informational (a shared counterparty); dashed grey: context. Hollow nodes were checked and set aside (sold, or too far out). Bars: equity per thesis area, orange is this check, the dashed red line is the 35.0% guideline.
Uses
2-hop conflict reachability over the commercial network COMMERCIAL: distance(from_=ConflictSubject), feeding portfolio exposure PORTFOLIO_EXPOSURE; current holdings only NORTHWIND_HOLDING; cross-fund conflict flag CONFLICT; the concentration rule, rolled up by sector closure CONCENTRATION.
Data: CommercialLink (COMMERCIAL_LINK), Ownership, Fund, PipelineEntry (PIPELINE, equity check), Sector.
Not SQL
The one-hop join counts any ownership row ever recorded and misses the shared counterparty; reach, "owned today" and a hierarchy rollup are not one query.

Add-on map Q-ADDON Backup, hidden tab Graph

Shows
Which companies best extend a Fund IV platform, judged by shared customers and suppliers rather than by sector label.
Read
Platform large in the centre; candidates sized by similarity and coloured by community; the side panel lists shared customers and suppliers; the state grid marks the whitespace states a candidate adds.
Uses
Jaccard similarity from each platform plus Louvain communities ADDON_SIMILARITY: jaccard_similarity, louvain over the commercial network COMMERCIAL.
Data: CommercialLink (COMMERCIAL_LINK), Ownership, company sites (COMPANY_SITE).
Not SQL
Neighbourhood similarity across a network is not a join; a sector screen ranks the same-niche decoy first.
Note
Reached at #addon, and only built when q_addon.json is exported. The current exports do not include it.

Act 1. Who fits and who is ready

2 min Q-SCORERulesExplorer: Scorecard

Type this in Claude Code

First type /clear and press Enter, so the act starts from an empty context (never between this prompt and its ad-lib).

Type this, verbatim
Which companies fit the Fund IV thesis and look ready to transact in the next 12 to 18 months? Show the Tier A list with the score components behind each one, and flag any that are not in our CRM.

Say while it runs

Fund IV is actively investing. The partners want a short list of companies that fit the Fund IV thesis today and are likely to transact soon, with every point of the score explained. Partners distrust black-box scores, so each point has to trace to a named rule and dated evidence. Most names on the list will have a banker engaged. Banker engaged is not process launched. It is the window to get in front of the book: a pre-empt, a seat in a limited process, or at least the first call when the teaser goes out.

Missed by the SQL screen:

  • FIXTURE Target Echo: FIXTURE. No keyword in its name.

Why a knowledge graph

The thesis is a tree with includes and an exclude at different levels, so fit needs recursion. Readiness is dated evidence across people, owners, funds and signals: a CFO who came from a company that was sponsor-backed while they were there is a three-way temporal join. The model keeps all of it as one governed definition that every later act reuses, with a reason attached to every point.

If live fails

  1. Say "let me pull the governed version" and type in Claude Code: Run uv run python ask.py q_score and show the result as a table with the why for each row.
  2. If Claude Code itself is down, in a second terminal: cd demo_workspace && uv run python ask.py q_score and talk over the printed table.
  3. If RAI or Snowflake is down, switch to the explorer, Scorecard view. It is built from the same exports and needs no network.

If step one fails because the engine, Snowflake or the network is down, keep Claude Code as the interface and type: Run uv run python ask.py --from-exports q_score and show the result as a table with the why for each row. It prints the same rows from the governed exports, labelled precomputed, with no engine. In the second terminal the same command works without Claude. Say "this is the governed export from this morning".

Hand-off

"Knowing who to call is half the job. The other half is who gets us in. Take the top 3."

Why a knowledge graph

"Knows" is derived by rules from overlapping tenure, deal co-work and positive CRM contact, each with dates and a strength. Path finding runs on that derived graph, so the path length can differ per target, every hop keeps its evidence, fresh ties outrank stale ones, and the same company at different times is not a relationship.

Elevator version (thirty seconds)

"Your deal team asks questions in plain English, and Claude answers them from one governed model of your deal universe that lives in your Snowflake: same definitions every time, every answer with its reasons. We asked who to call: it found 6 Tier A targets for Fund IV, 2 of them with no coverage. It found a warm route in for 2 of the top 3 and said honestly that one is cold. It showed that FIXTURE Boutique Gap bridges flow in your sectors and you barely cover it. Skeptic Q&A

Answer short, then offer to show it.

"Affinity or DealCloud already shows me warm intros."

Keep them; a path is one signal. Affinity knows who you know. It does not know FIXTURE Boutique Two is running FIXTURE Target Alpha, FIXTURE Boutique Gap is engaged on FIXTURE Target Charlie, or that FIXTURE Target Delta takes you over your FIXTURE Area One guideline. Here each path is weighted by tenure overlap and recency, false ties are rejected, and access is combined with fit, readiness and conflicts in one governed score. Affinity and PitchBook become inputs, not rivals.

"Half your Tier A list already has a banker. That's not sourcing."

Right, and the model knew a banker was engaged months before a teaser would reach you. The value is position: who on our team knows that banker (the warm-path act) and whether we are on their call list (the deal-flow act).

"DealCloud already has a scoring field."

A field an associate types is stale by Friday. This score is re-derived from dated facts every run, with the reason attached.

"Grata would have found FIXTURE Target Charlie."

Grata finds companies. It does not rank them by readiness and access with evidence, or check them against your portfolio.

"Where does debt maturity come from on a founder-owned company?"

Vendor debt data for sponsor-backed names, lender and banker conversations logged in the CRM, UCC filings. Where you do not have it, the point is not awarded, and the scorecard shows that.

"Does our deal data leave Snowflake?"

The data, the model and the reasoning stay in your account. Claude sees the results of the queries it runs, the answer rows on screen, not your tables. If those rows must stay inside the boundary too, Claude models are available inside Snowflake through Cortex.

From the domain brief:

"Our CRM data is a mess. Garbage in, garbage out."

Each score shows its components and evidence, so missing data appears as a missing component, not a silent zero. Start with three sources already in Snowflake: CRM, deal history, a vendor feed.

"Would I bet a deal on a score?"

No. It ranks who to call Monday and why; the rules are business language in your Snowflake, editable in a sentence. The opposite of a black box.
